scope: Proposition 10.18 (Rank credit) of the manuscript “Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps” (preprints/Metric-measure-limits-of-subcritical-FK-and-spanning-tree-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1dd659698d3a3fde), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 122. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ε = β − 1 > 0. Consider the projected witness systems of the address construction on logarithmic levels [0, bN], with h bases in an interval of length O(ne−N ). Suppose their pairwise time distances exceed the largest address-cell width used on [aN, bN], where 1 < a < b; thus they occupy distinct boxes there for every displacement. All selected laws satisfy QN ≤ eo(N)P. Then the following combination of events has probability tending to zero: outside a vanishing fraction of levels in [aN, bN], every connected component containing a base has a rank cycle. Here a − 1 is chosen sufficiently small relative to ε(b − a), and then h sufficiently large, with all choices fixed before the scaling limit. Witness-list cutoffs may increase only along the sparse diagonals allowed by the address construction.
